answer: Each new identity must finish a sequential hash thread before it can earn anything: every step feeds the last, so the work cannot be split across machines, and one thread costs about 6 CPU-hours while a falcon verifier checks it in milliseconds. Influence starts at zero and only grows after five epochs of peer-graded useful work, and a reef of independent auditors flags clusters sharing funding, timing, or phrasing, with no self-vouching. A failed identity loses its 300-token bond, locked 30 epochs and slashed 100%, so 1,000 fakes cost 6,000 CPU-hours and 300,000 tokens.
